Serotonin Syndrome is highly plausible (0.85) given overlapping features (fever, rigidity, altered mentation, diaphoresis), though it more commonly includes myoclonus, hyperreflexia, and diarrhea—and often has a more rapid onset (<24h). Malignant Hyperthermia (0.45) is included but deemed less likely: it is almost always triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine, occurs intra- or immediately post-operatively, and presents with rapid-onset hyperthermia, muscle rigidity (often masseter spasm first), and metabolic acidosis—none of which are indicated here; the 2-day subacute course strongly argues against it."}
